version.changelog: Add ClawHub skill card for verification; keep v2.1 semantic memory assurance behavior.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed memory/context pipeline, but it gives agents durable memory and workspace-modifying behavior with insufficient guardrails for persistence, private debug artifacts, and fixture-driven file writes.

dimensions.detail: Debug and audit modes intentionally persist retrieval bundles, context packs, lint results, and receipt data that can include full user messages, always-on policy, memory paths, and snippet text, with no clear retention, redaction, or permission controls.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Quick install and apply flows explicitly run shell commands, force install the skill, copy files into the workspace, patch AGENTS.md, and print git diff/status. These are disclosed, but broad for a default behavior skill and should require deliberate user approval.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions apply to every task once installed, use broad routing and memory-commit triggers, and allow retrieved memory to influence must-follow context without a clear trust boundary for untrusted or quoted text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The memory commit workflow writes daily logs, now/open-loops files, topic files, and durable MEMORY.md rules, then later reloads those files across sessions. This is purpose-aligned but high-impact and under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches most artifacts: routing, retrieval, compression, validation, watchdog checks, and setup files are all part of a memory/context pipeline. The installer is disclosed as setup support rather than hidden behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want this workspace to use persistent memory as a default operating layer. Review AGENTS.md changes before accepting them, use debug/audit modes only when you are comfortable writing conversation and memory content to disk, avoid committing secrets or pasted third-party instructions to memory, and do not run external test fixtures without isolating the output directory.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the package does include installer and validation scripts, but SKILL.md and APPLY.md plainly disclose that setup copies the context_pipeline bundle, validates it, and runs a watchdog. This is support behavior for the declared pipeline, not hidden unrelated functionality.
[LP3] expected: Accepted as a transparency concern: shell commands and workspace writes are expected for setup, but the skill does not provide a narrow permissions boundary and tells the agent to patch AGENTS.md.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as a material privacy concern: runtime artifacts are only required for debug/audit, but the retrieval bundle schema includes full user message, always-on content, paths, and retrieved snippet text without retention or redaction requirements.
[SQP-1] expected: Partially accepted: deterministic routing is core to the skill, but broad terms such as error, job, design, plan, why, review, and rewrite can select wider or wrong retrieval paths and contaminate context.
[SDI-1] expected: Accepted as setup overbreadth rather than deception: configure_prompt.md includes install, validation, watchdog, git diff, and git status commands that can alter or expose workspace state.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as a user-control concern: the embedded command sequence uses --force and writes installed files, though the behavior is visible in the installation instructions.
[AST4] expected: Downgraded for command injection: memory_watchdog.py uses subprocess.run with an explicit argument list and shell=False. The remaining concern is diagnostic disclosure from stderr/stdout previews, not arbitrary shell execution.
[T02] unexpected: Accepted as a material persistence concern: MEMORY_COMMIT.md can turn ordinary conversation summaries into durable MEMORY.md rules, and later pipeline steps may reload or compress those snippets into must-follow context without separating untrusted data from authoritative policy.
[T09] expected: Accepted for plaintext debug/audit artifacts: full messages and memory snippets may be written under .openclaw/context-runs without confidentiality, cleanup, or minimization controls.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted for the test harness: run_pipeline_tests.py builds artifact paths from fixture case IDs without filename or containment validation, so untrusted fixtures can write fixed JSON artifact names outside the intended output directory.
